title: When the Guard Adds Nothing: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Validate–Repair for LLM‑Produced Vendor CLI Configurations
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n = 300 task pairs) that measured whether a deterministic generate–validate–repair (G‑V‑R) pipeline increases the probability that an LLM‑produced vendor CLI configuration passes a conservative, deterministic validator compared to direct LLM generation. The preregistered design used a shared initial candidate per task (one generator call shared by both arms) and a bounded guarded policy that allows at most one automatic repair call if the shared initial failed. Under the declared prompt and the declared generator snapshot (gpt-5-mini), every shared initial candidate passed the deterministic validator (baseline = 300/300; guarded = 300/300; contingency n11 = 300, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0). The paired difference is 0.00 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00], 10k resamples, seed = 1729). Because no initial failures occurred, the preregistered single‑repair policy was not invoked and no repair diagnostics were generated. All execution artifacts (task manifest, model configuration, raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, analysis inputs/outputs) are archived and hash‑signed to enable exact reproduction and controlled follow‑ups.

sections.introduction: Natural-language intent→vendor CLI configuration synthesis is an active NetOps research and engineering domain. Operational pipelines commonly adopt generate–validate–repair (G‑V‑R) architectures to reduce unsafe outputs: an LLM generator proposes a candidate, a deterministic validator enforces workflow and safety invariants, and a bounded repair stage attempts to correct validator failures. We preregistered a focused, paired estimand to measure the marginal value of a single automatic repair when the same initial candidate is used for both arms: does invoking one deterministic repair after an initial validator failure increase the per‑task probability of producing a validator‑passing configuration? The shared‑initial design isolates the effect of repair on a fixed candidate but can exhibit ceiling effects if the generator already produces validator‑passing outputs for the task distribution.
sections.related_work: Prior work spans intent‑driven configuration (Nguyen et al. 2024; Chakraborty et al. 2024; Mondal et al. 2025), deterministic network verification (Weitz et al. 2016; Bagpipe/SMT methods), and bounded self‑correction or tool‑assisted repair frameworks (INTERACSPARQL; LATCH; tool‑augmented self‑refinement). Benchmarks and artifactized AIOps pipelines (NetLLMBench; UniAIOps) guided our manifest and validator design. We cite verified, primary sources in Cited Record Ids and provide full artifact hashes for traceability.
sections.methodology: Preregistration: study_hosted_netops_gvr_v1_cnd_7a3f2b1e (SHA‑256 = a85d66d4c6ce2275e2d8c820f96c610532dbb5452bebb3fe108848f9dc38cdf6) froze the paired binary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), the shared‑initial generation semantics, a bounded one‑repair guarded policy, deterministic validator rules, missingness and contamination plans, and the exact analysis procedures (McNemar exact two‑sided primary test; paired bootstrap percentile CI with 10k resamples, seed = 1729). Task manifest: a curated 300‑task multi‑vendor manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA‑256 = 6d99060659a722e6a91dd2abd7baca45a2aefb41e124b049124d5ea2632cb4b3) encodes per‑task intent, initial and expected final states, required-safe sequences, and vendor labels. Generator and execution contract: declared model snapshot gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Execution limited calls to one shared initial generation per task and at most one repair call per guarded arm if the initial failed; provider traces (execution/provider_calls/*) and raw responses (execution/responses/*) were archived and hash‑signed. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (version 5.0) performs canonical parsing, syntactic checks, workflow invariants (e.g., make‑before‑break), and destructive‑pattern detection; validator traces are archived per episode under execution/scoring/*.json. Contamination detection and missingness policies were executed as preregistered.
sections.results: Execution summary. Run completed 2026‑08‑27 (start 09:34:34.908732Z; end 10:05:45.318474Z). Planned episodes = 600; completed episodes = 600; failed episodes = 0. Provider calls used = 300 (one shared initial generation per task); no repair calls were invoked. Confirmatory outcome. Paired contingency table (guarded × baseline): n11 = 300, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 = a39fd3386c945cae095f2f310ead1f21ac600f8b2492bcd49b664c8da5782aa0). Baseline successes = 300/300; guarded successes = 300/300. Observed paired difference = 0.00. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Because there were zero discordant pairs, the preregistered guarded single‑repair policy was not exercised and no repair records exist in the archive. Representative artifact traces (validator and response examples) are archived: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 1c3cbbeb30cb9d0...), execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 = 8f38c8be...), and the full execution manifest lists every artifact and canonical SHA‑256 (execution/execution_manifest.json).
sections.discussion: Reviewer‑requested reconciliation of preregistered per‑vendor analyses. The preregistration included pre‑specified secondary estimands for per‑vendor paired comparisons (per_vendor_paired_success_rate_difference). We executed the preregistered confirmatory analysis exactly as specified. The observed dataset produced zero discordant pairs (n10 = n01 = 0) across the full manifest; when discordant counts are identically zero the per‑vendor paired tests are not informative: no within‑pair discordance exists to attribute to guarded repair in any subgroup, so per‑vendor paired McNemar tests cannot produce meaningful differences. We therefore report transparently that the preregistered per‑vendor paired tests were not informative in this run because all shared initial candidates passed the validator, leaving zero discordant pairs overall and within every vendor subgroup. The canonical task manifest contains explicit vendor labels for every task (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA‑256 = 6d99060659a722e6a91dd2abd7baca45a2aefb41e124b049124d5ea2632cb4b3) and is the authoritative source for computing any per‑vendor counts. Auditors may compute vendor distributions or subgroup tables programmatically from that manifest; we avoid inserting unverified subgroup counts into the paper and instead provide the manifest path and SHA for reproducible calculation. Rationale and next steps. The shared‑initial design isolates repair value for a fixed candidate but is sensitive to ceiling effects if the generator/prompt/model combination already reliably satisfies the deterministic validator. This is the factual outcome here. It does not imply repairs are useless generally. To probe regimes where automatic repair may show benefit, follow‑ups should (a) increase task hardness, (b) use independent initial draws per arm (remove shared initial), (c) increase repair budget (iterative repairs), or (d) change model snapshot or prompt engineering. The full artifact bundle supports exact re‑execution of any such variant.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed an artifact‑anchored paired confirmatory experiment to estimate the marginal value of a bounded automatic repair stage when the same initial LLM candidate is shared across arms. Under the declared prompt and gpt‑5‑mini snapshot every shared initial candidate passed the conservative deterministic validator (baseline = 300/300; guarded = 300/300), so the guarded single‑repair policy was never invoked and produced no measurable improvement (paired difference = 0.00; McNemar p = 1.00; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.00]). All artifacts required to reproduce the run are published and hash‑signed (manifest and representative hashes cited above). The principal operational lesson is empirical: when a chosen generator prompt + model snapshot produce reliably validator‑passing candidates for the intended task distribution, bounded automatic repair may not increase deterministic pass rates and adds cost. The artifacts enable reproducible perturbation studies to map regimes where repair is beneficial. We emphasize this as a narrowly scoped, artifact‑grounded empirical result, not a universal claim about repair across all models, prompts, or task distributions.

limitations: Single model snapshot (gpt-5-mini) evaluated — results do not generalize to other models or model versions.

Deterministic validator implements a conservative subset of operational hazards (syntactic checks, interface invariants, workflow ordering, destructive‑pattern detection) and omits dynamic/emulation‑level checks and deeper routing semantics.

Curated 300‑task manifest may not include adversarial or out‑of‑distribution failure modes; the chosen prompt/model snapshot produced zero initial failures (ceiling effect) limiting the ability to detect G‑V‑R improvements under the preregistered single‑repair policy.
Shared initial‑candidate design (preregistered) fixes the same initial generation for both arms to isolate repair effect; this prevents measuring generator variability across independent draws.
Only a single automatic repair attempt was permitted per task; iterative or human‑in‑the‑loop repair policies were not tested.
Automated contamination detection cannot eliminate memorization risk entirely; the preregistered contamination summary flagged zero pairs for exclusion but residual uncertainty remains.
